scope: Static audit of database/migrations/ + hot query-pattern grep in app/Http/Controllers, app/Services. V1 Le Cayenne LOCAL single-box file-driver MySQL. No EXPLAIN harness run — see Section 6 justification.
headline: At V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne (single branch, single-digit-k orders/day), every hot WHERE-clause is covered by at least one index — most by purpose-built composites added through the 2026-03 through 2026-05 perf waves. Six gaps identified are low-impact at V1 scale but become P1-P2 cost-tiers at the V2 SaaS multi-tenant + 1M+ orders horizon. None block V1 production. Sentinel skeleton written.

static_audit: Cross-reference each hot-WHERE in app/Services + app/Http/Controllers against the catalogued indexes
Verify column order on critical composites by reading the migration source
methodology.honest_limitation: EXPLAIN harness NOT executed — borrowing the framing from tests/Feature/Migrations/ActionLogsCompositeIndexTest.php line 14-15: 'the MySQL query planner behaviour on 500k rows belongs to a staging benchmark, not PHPUnit'. The dev DB is sqlite (RefreshDatabase). True planner verification requires a staging instance seeded to 1M-row scale. Tagged as V1.0.X cloud-prep gate.
scope_exclusions: Spatie permission_tables — vendor migration, self-managed indexes
Sanctum personal_access_tokens base schema — vendor, but FoodKing adds NO supplementary index on it (documented as gap below)

missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.rationale: KitchenDisplaySystemOrderService::historyToday (line 232) does WHERE branch_id AND updated_at BETWEEN [todayStart, tomorrowStart] ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 50. Currently has NO index supporting WHERE updated_at — MySQL falls back to (branch_id, status) leading column then row-by-row updated_at filter. At V1 Le Cayenne single-resto with <500 orders/day this is fine. At V2 SaaS with 100+ branches × 1000 orders/day per branch, the scan cost grows linearly per branch view.
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.regression_risk: LOW — additive index, write cost ~3-5% on UPDATE statements (orders.updated_at is touched on every status transition).
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.v1_local_impact: Negligible — Le Cayenne <500 orders/day, scan completes in <5ms.
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.v2_saas_impact: P1 — without it, every branch manager opening 'Historique' triggers a per-branch table scan growing with order count.

missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.missing_index: (dispatched_at, created_at)  OR  refactor DomainEvent::scopeStale to filter on occurred_at
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.rationale: DomainEvent::scopeStale (app/Models/DomainEvent.php:39-43) filters WHERE dispatched_at IS NULL AND created_at < ?. idx_pending covers (dispatched_at, occurred_at) — created_at and occurred_at are DIFFERENT columns (occurred_at is the domain timestamp, created_at is the row insert time). Cron foodking:outbox:retry-failed therefore can't fully use the index. Two equally good fixes: (a) add (dispatched_at, created_at) composite, or (b) refactor scopeStale to use occurred_at (semantically more correct — domain semantic is 'event happened > N min ago, still un-dispatched').
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.proposed_migration: OPTION A: $table->index(['dispatched_at', 'created_at'], 'idx_pending_created');  OPTION B: code change to DomainEvent.php scopeStale — replace 'created_at' with 'occurred_at'.
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.regression_risk: LOW for either path. Option B is preferred — no schema change, semantic alignment.
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.v1_local_impact: Negligible — outbox stays small (~10s rows pending typical).
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.v2_saas_impact: P2 — at outbox backlog of 100k+ during incident, full pending scan becomes minutes.

missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.missing_index: expires_at (or partial: WHERE expires_at IS NOT NULL)
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.rationale: sanctum:prune-expired daily cron (scheduled in app/Console/Kernel.php line 154) issues DELETE FROM personal_access_tokens WHERE expires_at IS NOT NULL AND expires_at < ?. Sanctum vendor migration does NOT index expires_at. At Le Cayenne kiosk-token TTL 480 min (CLAUDE.md §9) + ~10 kiosk tokens at once, table stays small — full scan OK V1. V2 SaaS multi-branch with relogin-on-shift kiosk pattern can pile up tens of thousands of expired tokens between cron runs.
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.regression_risk: LOW — additive. Write cost minimal (column rarely updated post-create).
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.v2_saas_impact: P2 — cron lock duration grows linearly with row count.

missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.rationale: OrderService::getOrders (line 255) does WHERE delivery_boy_id = $user->id. Column is bigInteger nullable (NOT foreignId-constrained — see migrations/2022_11_17_110810 line 38), so NO implicit FK index. Existing query falls back to full scan filtered by branch_id index (delivery boys are scoped). At V1 Le Cayenne with <5 delivery riders × <500 orders/day, scan is <10ms. At V2 SaaS with 20+ riders × 1000 orders/day per branch, becomes >100ms per rider screen refresh.
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.proposed_migration: Schema::table('orders', fn ($t) => $t->index('delivery_boy_id', 'idx_orders_delivery_boy'));  // optionally composite (delivery_boy_id, status) for active-tour filter.
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.v2_saas_impact: P2 — rider mobile app polls every 10s.

missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.rationale: Per-type aggregations (earn vs redeem totals) common in admin loyalty reports. UNIQUE(user_id, order_id, type) leading on user_id does NOT serve WHERE type alone. user_id solo index exists; type alone or composite (user_id, type) absent.
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.v2_saas_impact: P3 — reports remain ad-hoc, not hot-path.

missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.rationale: idx_order_items_order_id (2026_03_12_130000 line 59) duplicates the implicit FK index auto-created by ->foreignId('order_id')->constrained('orders') in the original 2022_11_17_110832 table create. Two indexes on the same single column add write penalty without read benefit.
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.proposed_action: OPTIONAL V1.0.X cleanup: drop idx_order_items_order_id (keep FK-implicit). Order: identify which index name MySQL uses for the FK CONSTRAINT (it auto-creates order_items_order_id_foreign), then DROP INDEX idx_order_items_order_id is safe.
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.regression_risk: LOW — keep test verifying FK index still present.
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.v2_saas_impact: P3 — at 10M+ order_items rows, double-index slows INSERT 10-15%.

missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.rationale: AuditLogService::lastHashFor (line 245) and FiscalChainValidator::verifyAuditChainTail (line 120) are the two chain-walk hot paths. Both filter WHERE branch_id then sort/window by id. MySQL handles this via branch_id index then PK back-reference — fine at V1 LOCAL audit_logs scale (Le Cayenne is currently 62 rows per MEMORY.md). At 10M+ rows V2 cloud-scale, an explicit (branch_id, id) composite eliminates the PK back-ref step.
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.regression_risk: LOW additive, BUT this is NF525-frozen table (CLAUDE.md §7) — requires LOCK plan even for an ADD INDEX. INSERT cost +5% (already-frozen NF525 write path tolerates this; chain-write is not throughput-critical).
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.v1_local_impact: Negligible — chain walk completes in <2ms at current 62-row scale.
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.v2_saas_impact: P2 — at 10M+ rows MySQL planner sometimes mis-orders index seek and falls back to filesort.

missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.issue: Task spec mentions 'customer_id' WHERE clause; schema uses 'user_id' (semantically the customer FK)
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.rationale: OrderService::posOrderStore line 699 stores customer_id INTO orders.user_id. idx_orders_user_id covers it. No gap, but naming inconsistency caught explicitly so future audits don't chase a non-existent column.
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.proposed_action: OPTIONAL doc-only: add comment in app/Models/Order.php :: $fillable explaining the user_id IS customer_id semantically (separate from creator_id which IS cashier). H.2-HEAL-02 wave already plans introducing creator_id (cashier column) per 2026_05_24 migration block-comment.

missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.missing_index: Task spec asks for (branch_id, status, created_at) 3-col compound — only 2-col (branch_id, status) present
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.rationale: Task #6 of the L6.2 brief explicitly asks the sentinel to assert (branch_id, status, created_at) compound. Currently idx_orders_branch_status is 2-col + idx_orders_datetime is 1-col. The 3-col index would serve:  (a) Z-report daily aggregation per branch+status range,  (b) admin 'orders by status for date range',  (c) sync-replay window filters. At V1 LOCAL the planner-merge of two indexes is adequate; at V2 SaaS the 3-col tightens range scans by 5-10x.
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.proposed_migration: Schema::table('orders', fn ($t) => $t->index(['branch_id', 'status', 'created_at'], 'idx_orders_branch_status_created'));  // SUPERSET of idx_orders_branch_status — could drop the 2-col after verifying no PHPUnit asserts the 2-col name explicitly.
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.regression_risk: MEDIUM — superset of existing 2-col, so could drop 2-col to avoid write penalty. BUT sentinel ActionLogsCompositeIndexTest pattern shows other tests assert exact index name presence — grep for 'idx_orders_branch_status' before dropping.
missing_indexes_recommendations_V1_0_X.v2_saas_impact: P1 — biggest single win for analytics + Z-report perf.
